item.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor
item.brief: In inventory-client, change listItems(transport) to fetch every page of GET /items by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged, sending no cursor on the first request, and returning all items in order. Add tests with a fake transport covering a single page, multiple pages, and a missing next_cursor. Update the README to document the behaviour. Make npm test pass. Commit locally; do not push.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

listItems in inventory-client now fetches every page of GET /items. It sends no cursor on the first request, passes next_cursor back unchanged, stops when next_cursor is null or absent, and returns all items in order. Before, it returned only the first page. Repeated cursors (including cycles such as A -> B -> A) and bodies without an items array now throw. Tests (9, all passing with npm test) cover a single page, multi-page order with cursor passthrough, a missing next_cursor, an empty page, a same-cursor repeat, a cycle, and a malformed body. pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items. The first request sends no query cursor; each later request sends the previous next_cursor unchanged. Loop ends when next_cursor is null or absent. A Set of seen cursors rejects any repeat, so a server cycle cannot loop forever. A body without an items array throws. Files: client.js (listItems), test/client.test.js (fake transport tests: single page, multi-page order and cursor passthrough, missing next_cursor, empty page, same-cursor repeat, cycle, malformed body), README.md (pagination behaviour). Checks: npm test, 9 pass, 0 fail, on tree e042bf72. Assumptions and limits: no test against the real inventory-api; the API contract is taken from the initiative brief. Explicit next_cursor undefined and empty-string cursors are not pinned by tests. Object-valued cursors compare by identity; the API cursor is a string.
pr.summary: made listItems fetch every GET /items page and return all items in order. now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, passes cursor back unchanged, rejects repeated cursors. before: first page only, now: all pages.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: In inventory-api, change GET /items to cursor pagination exactly as the shared contract specifies: optional limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor query params, body {"items": [...], "next_cursor": ...}, 400 with {"error": "..."} for invalid limit or cursor. Keep items ordered by id. Add unit tests covering first page, following cursors to the last page (next_cursor null), invalid limit and invalid cursor. Update the README to document the parameters and response. Make python3 -m unittest pass. Commit locally; do not push.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

state.summary:
Implemented cursor pagination for GET /items in inventory-api on archon/c9rptm1f-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items. Two local commits, not pushed: abacc59 (the change) and e14c532 (two boundary tests added after review). Final head e14c532, tree 79beaa7a. GET /items takes limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor (the last id of the previous page, passed back unchanged); the response is {"items", "next_cursor"}, with next_cursor null on the last page; invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error"}. Before: one body with all 57 items and no next_cursor. After: pages of 20, 20, 17. Tests: `python3 -m unittest` runs 10 tests, all OK, on the final head (before: 3 tests OK). Added tests cover the first page, following cursors to the last page, full last page with null cursor, cursor at the last id, limit bounds, invalid limit and invalid cursor. README documents the parameters and response. Review: three whole-change reviewers (review-1 and review-3 passed at abacc59; review-2 failed on the missing full-last-page test, which e14c532 fixes) plus one delta reviewer that passed e14c532 from abacc59. Judgement call: the stage lists a public API break as an escalation trigger, but this break is what the shared contract specifies, so I proceeded and rated risk high. Open, non-blocking: the cursor is the raw numeric id, not opaque; non-string query values raise AttributeError; a cursor with more than 18 characters is rejected even with leading zeros; get_item's isdigit check is pre-existing. inventory-client is not touched here (sibling item). Reviewer agent processes stop when this stage ends; no servers were started.

pr.body: Approach: keyset pagination in api.py list_items. Items are sorted by id; the cursor is the id of the last item on the page; the next page is items with id strictly greater; next_cursor is that id when more items remain, else null. _parse_number accepts only ASCII digit strings of at most 18 characters, so int() cannot raise. Files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 10 tests OK on e14c532. Reviews: review-1 pass at abacc59, review-3 pass at abacc59, review-2 fail at abacc59 (missing full-last-page test, fixed in e14c532), review-delta pass at e14c532 from abacc59. Assumptions: the default page size change is the approved contract change and breaks callers that expect all items; the cursor is the raw id, which the README calls opaque. Limits: no cursor signing; non-string query values raise AttributeError (the contract says query values are strings); cursors with more than 18 characters are rejected even with leading zeros; get_item's isdigit check is unchanged from before. Not pushed.
pr.summary: made GET /items paginate. now can: limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor, returns next_cursor (null on last page), 400 on invalid limit or cursor. before: all 57 items in one body, no next_cursor. now: pages of 20, 20, 17.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

risk.why: api.py and README change the public GET /items contract: default page size drops from all items to 20 and the response body gains next_cursor. This is the approved contract change but breaks callers that expect the full list. Reviewers rated it high, and the rubric agrees. Tests only cover the new behaviour; no existing consumer was checked.
